I’m sorry—I don’t have the ability to pull up‑to‑date weather information directly from the web right now. Below is a quick guide on how you can obtain exactly what you’re looking for yourself: --- ### 1️⃣ Pick a Public Forecast Service | Provider | Free Tier / Key Needed | Typical Endpoint | |----------|------------------------|------------------| | **Open-Meteo** | ✅ No key required | https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast | | **WeatherAPI.com** | ❌ Key needed (free tier available) | http://api.weatherapi.com/v1/forecast.json | | **NOAA Climate Data Online** | ❌ Key needed | https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/cdo-web/api/v2/data | For most hobbyist projects, *Open‑Meteo* works great because it’s completely public and doesn’t require authentication. --- ### 2️⃣ Build Your Request URL (Example – Open‑Meteo) ```text https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast? latitude=37.8651& longitude=-119.5383& daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min& # optional daily summary hourly=temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability& start_date=YYYY-MM-DD& end_date=YYYY-MM-DD& timezone=auto ``` #### Parameters Explained | Parameter | Description | |-----------|-------------| | `latitude` & `longitude` | Coordinates of your location (`37.8651`, `-119.5383`) | | `hourly=` | Comma‑separated list of variables you want each hour. For your case:
`temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability` | | `start_date` | First day of the period you want (format `yyyy-mm-dd`). | | `end_date` | Last day of the period you want (same format). | | `timezone` | Set to `auto` so the service uses local time at the given lat/lon. | > **Tip:** If you just want “next 10 days” starting today, set `start_date` to today's date and `end_date` to `today + 9`. --- ### 3️⃣ Example Call Using Python (`requests`) ```python import datetime from urllib.parse import urlencode import requests lat, lon = 37.8651, -119.5383 base_url = "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast" params = { "latitude": lat, "longitude": lon, "hourly": "temperature_2m,windspeed_10m,precipitation_probability", "daily": "weathercode", # optional extra field "timeformat": "iso8601", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", } # Compute dates today = datetime.date.today() end_day = today + datetime.timedelta(days=9) params["start_date"] = today.isoformat() params["end_date"] = end_day.isoformat() url = f"{base_url}?{urlencode(params)}" print("Request URL:", url) response = requests.get(url) data = response.json() # <-- contains all requested values print(data.keys()) # shows top-level keys like 'hourly', 'daily' ``` This script will return a JSON object containing arrays for each variable over the specified range—perfect for feeding into a spreadsheet, database, or visualisation pipeline. --- ### 4️⃣ What You’ll Get Back (Typical Structure) ```json { "hourly_units": { "time":"ISO8601", "temperature_2m":"°C", "windspeed_10m":"km/h", "precipitation_probability":"%" }, "hourly": { "time":["2026-05-17T00:00","2026-05-17T01:00", ...], "temperature_2m":[12.5,11.8,...], "windspeed_10m":[15.0,14.7,...], "precipitation_probability":[20,18,...] } } ``` Each array aligns by index, meaning element `i` across all lists corresponds to the same timestamp. --- ### 5️⃣ Handling Time Zones & Daylight Saving If you’d rather work purely in UTC timestamps, replace `"timezone"` with `"UTC"`. Otherwise keep `"auto"` or specify something like `"America/Los_Angeles"` to automatically adjust for daylight saving changes during the ten‑day window. --- ### 6️⃣ Next Steps 1. **Run the above script locally** (you’ll need Python ≥ 3.6 and the `requests` package). 2. **Parse the returned JSON** to extract the three columns you care about: - Temperature (`temperature_2m`) - Wind Speed (`windspeed_10m`) - Precipitation Probability (`precipitation_probability`) 3. **Store or display** them however suits your workflow (CSV export, Pandas dataframe, chart, etc.). --- ### 📚 Quick Reference Table (Variables Available from Open‑Meteo) | Variable | Unit | Notes | |----------|------|-------| | `temperature_2m` | °C | Air temp at ~2 meters | | `windspeed_10m` | km/h | Horizontal wind speed at ~10 m | | `precipitation_probability` | % | Chance of rain/snow per hour | | `relativehumidity_2m` | % | Relative humidity | | `dewpoint_2m` | °C | Dew point temperature | | …and many more… | — | See [Open‑Meteo docs](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs) | Feel free to tweak the parameters until you hit the exact granularity you need!
